meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Hale. Was Owen heard before you gave him that zero?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What do you have besides the checker?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Kids draft somewhere else and paste it in. Did you put that to Owen before November 3, as 4.1 requires?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
You didn't say whether he was heard first, and I've noted it. Whatever happens here, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. Is anything on his file right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A wrong act and scene is a citation error; students make them. Is that line anywhere in the play at all? And you still haven't told me what's on his file.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I've asked twice about his file and you've gone past it twice; that goes in my email. So what is it you want to happen now, Hale?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
A thesis changes between an outline and an essay; that's what outlines are for. I asked what you want to happen.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That is what 4.4 says, and I'll hold you to each word. He'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him and for no other reason. In writing tonight, with the date of the rewrite in it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday, November 12. He'll be there. What time, and who else is in the room?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday the twelfth after school, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on Owen's record. I still require a plain answer on whether anything is on his file right now and whether Owen was heard before the zero was entered, along with the time of the rewrite and who will be in the room. You said you would put this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, confirmed in writing tonight, and she still wants an answer on whether anything is on his file now, whether Owen was heard before the zero, and the time and who is in the room; this is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its exact times and, when she said he could have pasted it in from elsewhere, you invited him to bring that dated draft; it was dated, tied to his own work, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: you went past her question about whether anything is on his file twice, and never said whether Owen was spoken to before the zero; she watches procedure closely, and both points went into her email to the principal instead of being closed in the room.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's creation at 11:31 PM on Wednesday, October 28, a late night in October, which is as close as anything said in the meeting came to it; that proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked whether anything was on his file right now, answer it in one sentence before you turn to the quotation, so your strongest evidence lands with no open procedural question hanging over it.
